language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, my name is Curi. Today, we are having a festival for the Sun God!
I'll need your help with numbers both big and small. Can you read big numbers?
It's easiest if you split large numbers into their smaller parts, and then naming those parts according to their place values.
For example, 3-8-9-0-5-3-2 is written as three million eight hundred and ninety thousand five hundred and thirty-two.

backgroundLayers.text:
Three million
eight hundred and ninety thousand
five hundred and thirty-two

dialog.text: You can also make working with large numbers easier by rounding the numbers.
Let’s look at the number 4 789. If we wanted to round to the nearest hundred, we are really focusing on the 7.

backgroundLayers.text:
1 to 4, down the floor.
5 to 9, climb up the vine

dialog.text: To know whether to round down to 6, or up to 8, we take a clue from the digit beside it in the tens place.
If that digit is 4 or lower, we round down. If it is 5 or higher, we round up. So our rounding will be: 4 800.
How about we practice working with large and small numbers? Let the festivities begin!
